arguments.summary: Conditional company contribution: NVDA’s FY27 grid tests whether guided AI-infrastructure demand can carry the second half; MU’s FY26 grid is dominated by the imminent guided Q4 completion and is more exposed to memory pricing/margin normalization. QQQ provides diversified but material dated overlap with both issuers; its sponsor aggregate P/E is not methodologically interchangeable with the assumed corporate P/Es.

claims.text: NVDA reported H1 FY27 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.85. The FY27 bear/base/bull assumptions of $8/$10/$12 leave constant-share residual EPS of $3.15/$5.15/$7.15 for Q3+Q4. Q3 guidance is $108bn revenue ±2%, 74% GAAP gross margin ±50bp and $9.2bn GAAP opex, without China Data Center compute revenue. Thus the $5.15 base residual requires guided Q3 plus a meaningful Q4 contribution; the $3.15 bear is a demand/mix/margin deceleration stress, while $7.15 requires Q3 upside and continued platform-ramp demand. Residuals are not exact annual reconciliations because reported and future diluted share bases differ.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, NVDA’s conditional bear/base/bull sensitivities are -28.02%/+12.48%/+61.97%. The base grid’s break-even threshold is 22.227x on assumed $10 EPS, or $8.8908 EPS at the assumed 25x—so the dated price is exceeded only if either threshold is achieved. The asymmetry comes from joint EPS and multiple changes, not a probability or fair-value conclusion. A Q3 result/guidance that fails to sustain the demand/margin bridge would reverse the base case; conversely, sustained ramp evidence and Q4 support would challenge the bear stress. The 20x/25x/30x bands are assumptions, not observed or normal multiples.

MU reported nine-month FY26 GAAP diluted EPS of $41.40 and guided Q4 GAAP EPS of $30.73 ±$1.00. The $65/$72/$78 annual scenarios imply constant-share Q4 residuals of $23.60/$30.60/$36.60: base approximately completes guidance, bear tests weaker memory demand/pricing or margin/cost pressure, and bull requires an AI-memory demand/margin beat above guidance. This is particularly near-term testable because MU scheduled fiscal Q4 results for September 30; residuals remain constant-share approximations, not exact annual EPS reconciliations.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, MU’s conditional bear/base/bull sensitivities are -36.01%/-0.77%/+38.22%. The base grid’s break-even threshold is 14.1083x on assumed $72 EPS, or $72.5571 EPS at the assumed 14x. Hence merely delivering the base operating completion leaves little conditional cushion under the selected multiple; the downside is larger than the upside because the bear combines a Q4 earnings shortfall with 10x compression, whereas bull combines a beat with 18x. This tests cycle-normalization risk rather than establishing any multiple as fair, likely, or historically normal.

QQQ’s dated sponsor holdings show NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336% of reported assets as of 2026-09-18; together they are 13.547564% before considering other related semiconductor holdings. QQQ’s sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of 2026-08-31. QQQ therefore retains direct exposure to both company earnings drivers but is not equivalent to either single-issuer grid; the fund P/E is an aggregate sponsor metric and cannot validate or rank the assumed issuer P/Es.

Within these conditional grids, MU has the more event-concentrated operating test because its FY26 base depends on a single guided Q4 that is scheduled to report shortly, while NVDA’s base depends on guided Q3 plus an unreported Q4 demand continuation. Both are less diversified than QQQ, which has dated exposure to each but also 103 reported holdings. This is a risk-structure comparison only, not a directional preference or return forecast.

gaps.description: No empirical issuer multiple history, consensus, or forward post-Q4/FY27 earnings evidence is supplied. This prevents an unconditional valuation ranking or a claim that any scenario P/E is fair, normal, or likely; it does not invalidate the explicitly assumed sensitivity grids.

No quantified current company exposure to China/export restrictions, customer concentration, or supply disruption is supplied in this role’s inputs. Policy impacts can be described only as conditional risks, not modeled into EPS or used to rank the companies against QQQ.

assumptions: All grid EPS and P/E inputs are scenario assumptions, not consensus, forecasts, fair values, probabilities, or observed issuer multiples.
Scenario residual EPS uses a constant diluted-share approximation; it does not silently combine different actual diluted-share counts.
Dated closes are split-adjusted completed-session observations; the company fiscal periods extend beyond the 63-session research horizon.
QQQ holdings and aggregate valuation are dated sponsor reporting, not current holdings or a corporate earnings model.
arguments.counter_thesis: AI infrastructure and memory demand could remain stronger than these stress cases, supporting results above guidance; alternatively, earnings could meet guidance yet the assumed multiple compresses, showing that operating execution and valuation risk are distinct. Conversely, QQQ’s diversification does not eliminate correlated AI/semiconductor exposure because it held both issuers and other related names.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA after the next reported quarter: reassess the base bridge if reported revenue/margin or forward outlook no longer supports the Q3-guidance-plus-Q4 residual mechanism; this would weaken the $10 EPS/25x conditional case.

Review MU upon its scheduled fiscal Q4 release: compare reported GAAP diluted EPS and outlook with the $30.60 base residual and $30.73 ±$1.00 guidance; a material shortfall changes the base completion premise and activates the memory-cycle downside mechanism.

Refresh QQQ sponsor holdings and aggregate valuation before relying on overlap: a material change in NVDA/MU weights or aggregate P/E changes the diversification and look-through comparison, without changing either company’s reported earnings facts.

shared_exposures.mechanism: AI-infrastructure demand can transmit through NVDA compute platforms and MU memory demand; QQQ had direct dated holdings in both issuers, so it is not a clean exclusion of that theme.
shared_exposures.qualification: QQQ weights are dated 2026-09-18 sponsor holdings and are not portfolio weights; the supplied data does not quantify correlated exposures across all other fund constituents.
